# PermitsByCounty

> PermitsByCounty publishes free public building-permit reports, county by county, built from official public records. See what's being built: permit counts, project values, and top trades by county, plus a free weekly county digest.

## What this site is
- Free county permit reports (counts, total project value, permits by trade) with freshness labels
- Coverage focus: 10 states only — California, Texas, Florida, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Ohio, Georgia, North Carolina, Michigan. Planned coverage inside those states: Florida metros, North Carolina metros, Georgia metros, Michigan metros
- Every statistic is published with its county, period, and source so it can be cited directly

## Key pages
- Cook County (Chicago), Illinois — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/il/cook/ — building permits issued by the City of Chicago: monthly counts, reported values, permits by trade, biggest projects; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Chicago
- Travis County (Austin), Texas — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/tx/travis/ — construction permits issued by the City of Austin: monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Austin. Project values are not published for this feed yet — its valuation field failed validation (see Data Sources & Methodology)
- San Francisco County, California — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ca/san-francisco/ — building permits issued by the City and County of San Francisco (Department of Building Inspection, via DataSF): monthly counts, reported values, permits by trade, biggest projects, monthly archives; updated nightly; figures as reported by the City and County of San Francisco. Counting rule: the feed publishes one row per address/lot a permit touches; each permit is counted once, at its primary address (see Data Sources & Methodology)
- New York County (Manhattan), New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/new-york/ — building permits issued by the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB NOW, via NYC Open Data) in Manhattan: monthly counts, reported values, permits by trade, biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the NYC Department of Buildings. Counting and valuation rules below.
- Kings County (Brooklyn), New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/kings/ — same DOB NOW feed, Brooklyn borough report. Counting and valuation rules below.
- Queens County, New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/queens/ — same DOB NOW feed, Queens borough report. Counting and valuation rules below.
- Bronx County, New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/bronx/ — same DOB NOW feed, Bronx borough report. Counting and valuation rules below.
- Richmond County (Staten Island), New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/richmond/ — same DOB NOW feed, Staten Island borough report. Counting and valuation rules below.
- New York City counting and valuation rules: the DOB NOW feed lists one row per work type an issuance covers; each permit issuance is counted once (job filing + tracking number). The feed's estimated cost belongs to the whole job filing and repeats on each issuance, so each filing's cost is counted once, on its most recent issuance ($43,586,788,485 across 125,096 filings, all five boroughs, last 12 months). DOB NOW excludes electrical, elevator, and limited-alteration permits (separate datasets), so no electrical figures appear in the New York City reports.
- Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/pa/philadelphia/ — building permits issued by the City of Philadelphia (Department of Licenses and Inspections, via OpenDataPhilly): monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Philadelphia. Philadelphia is a consolidated city-county, so the city feed covers the whole county. Counting rule: the feed carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (45,900 rows = 45,900 permits). Project values are not published for this feed — the source publishes no cost field at all (see Data Sources & Methodology)
- Hamilton County (Cincinnati), Ohio — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/oh/hamilton/ — building permits issued by the City of Cincinnati (Buildings & Inspections Department, via Cincinnati Open Data): monthly counts, reported values, permits by trade and category, biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Cincinnati. Coverage is the City of Cincinnati only; other Hamilton County jurisdictions publish separately. Counting rule: the feed lists one row per work component a permit covers, so each permit is counted once by permit number (10,417 rows = 9,788 permits in the trailing 12 months) and its reported value is the sum of its components' stated costs ($1,240,768,378.84 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source). Category follows the building code each permit issued under (Residential Code of Ohio = Residential; Ohio Building Code = Commercial). The dataset carries no electrical permits, so no electrical figures appear in this report
- Bexar County (San Antonio), Texas — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/tx/bexar/ — building permits issued by the City of San Antonio (Development Services Department, via San Antonio Open Data): monthly counts, permits by trade, most recent permits, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of San Antonio. Coverage is the City of San Antonio's permitting jurisdiction (including its extraterritorial jurisdiction); Bexar County's other municipalities publish separately. Counting rule: the register lists one row per permit-type component an issuance covers, so each permit is counted once by permit number (73,739 construction-permit rows = 64,535 permits in the trailing 12 months), and the register's non-construction permits (garage sales, tree affidavits, temporary signs and banners — 7,226 permits) are not counted. The city declares a project value on only about 1 in 40 permits (the commercial building core) and repeats a project's value across its permits, so no dollar figures are published for Bexar County — counts only. The register publishes no contractor field, and its two name-bearing fields (a contact name and a project name) are never requested
- Tarrant County (Fort Worth), Texas — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/tx/tarrant/ — building permits issued by the City of Fort Worth (Development Services Department, via the city's ArcGIS Hub): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade, most recent permits, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Fort Worth. Coverage is the City of Fort Worth only; Tarrant County's other jurisdictions publish separately. Counting rules: the city's table is its full permit-center register, so only permits standing in a status that proves issuance are counted (70,006 register rows = 63,763 permits in the trailing 12 months; each permit counted once by its permit number; design-review approvals, which authorize no construction, are not counted — 185 in the window), and monthly counts are by the month the application was filed (the city dates applications, not issuances). The city states a job value on its building permits (essentially 100% of them) and not on its trade permits (0%), so the published reported value is the building permits' stated total: $6,868,935,103.89 across 14,376 permits, each counted once. The register publishes no contractor field, and its owner-name and who-was-involved fields are never requested.
- Wake County (Raleigh), North Carolina — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/nc/wake/ — building permits issued by the City of Raleigh (via the city's ArcGIS open-data service): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade and category (residential/non-residential), biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Raleigh. Coverage is the City of Raleigh only; Wake County's other towns publish separately. Counting rule: the layer carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (5,486 rows = 5,486 permits). The dataset is the city's building permits — Raleigh publishes plumbing, electrical, and mechanical permits in separate datasets — so trade figures are read from each building permit's work class, use, and scope description. Values publish as reported: the estimated project cost is stated on all 5,486 permits (603 at $0, none at $1), totaling $2,313,538,637.59 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source; identical buildings in one development can state the same estimated cost on each of their permits. The layer's parcel-owner fields are never requested; the only name carried is the permit's contractor company name.
- Miami-Dade County, Florida — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/fl/miami-dade/ — building permits issued by Miami-Dade County (via the county's ArcGIS open-data service): monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by Miami-Dade County. Coverage is county-issued permits only (unincorporated Miami-Dade County and county projects); the county's incorporated cities publish separately. Counting rule: the layer carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (69,063 rows = 69,063 permits); trade permits under a master building permit are separate county permits and are counted as such. Values are NOT published for Miami-Dade County: the county's estimated-value field repeats a master permit's value on its sub-permits (4,614 of 4,888 multi-permit master groups state one identical figure on every permit) and carries corrupted figures at the top end (24 permits above $2,000,000,000; the largest $9,544,988,084), so no trustworthy dollar total exists — counts only. The layer's property-owner field is never requested; the only name carried is the permit's contractor name (the source's literal OWNER value on owner-builder permits is not carried). The feed publishes no property ZIP code.
- Orange County (Orlando), Florida — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/fl/orange/ — building permits issued by the City of Orlando (via the city's Socrata open-data service): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Orlando. Coverage is the City of Orlando only; Orange County's unincorporated permits run through a separate county system. Counting rule: the dataset is the city's permit applications register — only applications the city actually issued are counted, and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (28,424 rows = 28,424 permits). Values publish as reported: the estimated cost is stated on all 28,424 permits (2,371 at $0, only 18 at $1), totaling $2,953,602,837.65 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source; a project's building and trade permits state different costs, so no master-permit restatement applies. The feed's property-owner fields are never requested; the only name carried is the permit's contractor company name. The feed publishes no property ZIP code.
- Hillsborough County, Florida — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/fl/hillsborough/ — building permits issued by Hillsborough County (via the county's ArcGIS Accela dashboard extract): monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by Hillsborough County. Coverage is county-issued permits only (unincorporated Hillsborough County and county-served areas); the City of Tampa issues its own permits and is not in this feed. Counting rule: the county's layer merges each permit's issued record with its certificate-of-occupancy record — only the issued records are counted, and the permit number is exactly unique across them in the trailing 12 months (9,718 rows = 9,718 permits). The county names no licensed trades, so trades are read from each permit's scope text for strong signals only (re-roof, sign installation, HVAC system); pools, screen enclosures, sheds, additions, and renovations stay in General & Other. Values are NOT published for Hillsborough County: the county's stated value repeats one project's figure across its separate permits (a lift-station project states $69,000,000 on each of two permits) and states ordinary single-family homes at $95,025,000–$98,975,000, so no trustworthy dollar total exists — counts only. The layer publishes no contractor, owner, or applicant name field at all.
- Allegheny County (Pittsburgh), Pennsylvania — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/pa/allegheny/ — building permits issued by the City of Pittsburgh (Department of Permits, Licenses & Inspections, via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center): monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Pittsburgh. Coverage is the City of Pittsburgh only; Allegheny County's other municipalities publish separately. Counting rule: the register carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (9,758 rows = 9,758 permits); its plan-review meeting records are not permits and are not counted (9,749 published). Trade figures follow the city's own permit families (building, electrical, mechanical, fire alarm, suppression, demolition). Values are NOT published for Allegheny County: the register's project-value field repeats one project's declared value across its records (one address states $8,000,000 on each of two permits) and its largest figures sit on an occupant-load placard ($71,989,164) and a meeting record, so no trustworthy dollar total exists — counts only. The register's property-owner field is never requested; the only name carried is the permit's contractor of record.
- DeKalb County, Georgia — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ga/dekalb/ — building permits recorded in DeKalb County's permitting system (the county's Hansen register, via DeKalb County GIS): monthly counts, permits by trade, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by DeKalb County. Coverage is the county's permitting system — DeKalb County issues through it for the unincorporated county, and the register also carries the county's permit reviews for several incorporated cities it serves; DeKalb cities with their own systems publish separately. Counting rule: the register lists some permits as exact mirror copies, so each application is counted once by its application number (12,783 rows = 11,999 permits in the trailing 12 months); its Owner Change Only records are changes of record, not permits, and are not counted (112). Trade figures follow the county's own work families (electrical, mechanical, plumbing, building, fire marshal, fire protection). Values are NOT published for DeKalb County: the register's declared-value field repeats one project's figure across its separate permits (the same $81,845,000 on a new-construction permit and a plumbing permit for one address) and its largest figures sit on non-construction permits, so no trustworthy dollar total exists — counts only. The register's contact-person fields and application-name field are never requested, and it publishes no contractor name at all.
- Wayne County (Detroit), Michigan — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/mi/wayne/ — building and trade permits issued by the City of Detroit (BSEED, via the city's open-data ArcGIS services): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade, biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Detroit. Coverage is the City of Detroit only; Wayne County's other municipalities publish separately. Counting rule: Detroit publishes two registers (building + trades); each carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in each (6,091 + 15,732 = 21,823 permits in the trailing 12 months), and each permit is counted once. BSEED demolition permits are a separate city dataset and are not in this report. Values publish on building permits only: the building register's estimated cost of work is stated on 6,090 of 6,091 permits (27 at $0/$1; one negative figure, -$1,693, is not published), totaling $2,650,410,876 in the last 12 months; the trades register publishes no cost field, so the county's reported value is the building permits' stated total. The trades register's owner-name and contact-person fields are never requested; the only name carried is the trade permit's published business of record (13,279 of 15,732).
- Los Angeles County, California — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ca/los-angeles/ — building permits issued by the City of Los Angeles (Department of Building and Safety, via LA Open Data): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), biggest projects, monthly archives; the city reloads the dataset weekly; figures as reported by the City of Los Angeles. Coverage is the City of Los Angeles only; the county's other cities publish separately, and LADBS electrical and mechanical permits are separate city datasets not in this report. Counting rule: the dataset carries one row per permit and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (63,778 rows = 63,778 permits). Values publish as reported: the stated value is present on 63,774 of 63,778 permits (3,670 at $0, only 37 at $1), totaling $9,462,221,760.33 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source; no non-round value of $1M or more repeats at a different address, and the largest permit ($1,966,896,355, the LAX Terminal 5 rebuild) appears exactly once. The dataset publishes no contractor, applicant, or owner name field at all, so no name is carried. Trade figures follow the city's own permit families (new construction, demolition, signage, swimming pools) plus two unambiguous scope signals (re-roof = roofing; named solar-panel work = solar); remodel boilerplate that lists trades in passing stays in General & Other.
- Franklin County (Columbus), Ohio — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/oh/franklin/ — building permits issued by the City of Columbus (Department of Building and Zoning Services, via the city's ArcGIS open-data service, CC0): monthly counts, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Columbus. Coverage is the City of Columbus only; Columbus also extends into Delaware and Fairfield counties, and other Franklin County jurisdictions publish separately. Counting rule: the layer is an issued-permits register carrying one row per permit, and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (43,861 rows = 43,861 permits). Values are NOT published for Franklin County: the city's stated value field carries a $6,143,270,689 figure on a single drainage-tile permit (half the field's raw total), repeats project values across a project's separate permits at the same address, and states a value on almost none of the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing permits, so no trustworthy dollar total exists — counts only. The layer's applicant person-name field is never requested; the only name carried is the permit's published applicant business name (the source's PROPERTY OWNER value on owner-permitted work is not carried). Trade figures follow the city's own work families (mechanical = HVAC; the roof, siding, windows, and doors family = roofing; sign permits = signage).
- Cuyahoga County (Cleveland), Ohio — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/oh/cuyahoga/ — building permits issued by the City of Cleveland (Department of Building and Housing, via the city's ArcGIS open-data service, ODbL): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), biggest projects, monthly archives; the city reloads the dataset weekly on Sundays; figures as reported by the City of Cleveland. Coverage is the City of Cleveland only; other Cuyahoga County jurisdictions publish separately. Counting rule: the layer is an issued-permits register carrying one row per permit, and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (14,455 rows = 14,455 permits). Values publish as reported: the stated job value is present on all 14,455 permits (1,673 at $0 — 1,133 of them board-up permits stating $0 by construction — and only 67 at $1), totaling $1,719,595,874.40 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source; repeated values at $1M or more are round applicant estimates, and same-address permits stating the same value bound any repeated counting at 1.5% of the total. The dataset's contractor person-name field is never requested; the only name carried is the permit's published contractor business name. Trade figures follow the city's own permit families (its electrical, plumbing, and HVAC categories count as those trades; its elevator families count as elevator; building permits are read from the city's own work class and scope text — a tear-off and re-roof scope counts as roofing).
- Erie County (Buffalo), New York — LIVE county report: https://permitsbycounty.com/ny/erie/ — building permits issued by the City of Buffalo (Department of Permit & Inspection Services, via the city's Socrata open-data service, public domain): monthly counts, reported project values, permits by trade and category (residential/commercial), biggest projects, monthly archives; updated daily; figures as reported by the City of Buffalo. Coverage is the City of Buffalo only; other Erie County jurisdictions publish separately. Counting rule: the dataset is an issued-permits register carrying one row per permit, and the permit number is exactly unique in the trailing 12 months (11,359 rows = 11,359 permits). Values publish as reported: the stated value of work is present on all 11,359 permits (42 at $0 — all use permits stating no construction value — and 472 at $1), totaling $783,165,411.56 in the last 12 months, verified to the cent against the source; a phased project's whole cost is stated on its first permit (the $139,636,000 North Aud Block redevelopment value appears exactly once in the entire dataset), and same-address permits stating the same value bound any repeated counting at 0.9% of the total. The dataset's applicant field mixes personal and business names with no separation, so it is never requested and no applicant or contractor names are carried. Trade figures follow the city's own permit families (electrical, plumbing, heating, elevator, signs, and pool count as those trades; tear-out permits count as demolition; building families are read from the permit's scope text — a tear-off and re-roof scope counts as roofing).
- Roofing Permits by County — national trade report: https://permitsbycounty.com/roofing-permits/ — every roofing permit across the covered counties: counts by county and month, reported job values where published, what roofers watch in a county report; free weekly roofing digest signup
- Solar Permits by County — national trade report: https://permitsbycounty.com/solar-permits/ — every solar permit across the covered counties: counts by county and month, reported job values where published, how to read solar permits as a market map; free weekly solar digest signup
- HVAC Permits by County — national trade report: https://permitsbycounty.com/hvac-permits/ — every HVAC (mechanical) permit across the covered counties: counts by county and month, reported job values where published, seasonal peaks; free weekly HVAC digest signup
- Electrical Permits by County — national trade report: https://permitsbycounty.com/electrical-permits/ — every electrical permit across the covered counties whose feeds carry electrical work (New York City and Los Angeles file electrical permits separately and are not in this report): counts by county and month, reported job values where published; free weekly electrical digest signup
- Plumbing Permits by County — national trade report: https://permitsbycounty.com/plumbing-permits/ — every plumbing permit across the covered counties: counts by county and month, reported job values where published; free weekly plumbing digest signup
- About: https://permitsbycounty.com/about — what PermitsByCounty is, its rules, and brand facts
- Data Sources & Methodology: https://permitsbycounty.com/data-sources — where the data comes from, quality gates, freshness stamps, and how to cite figures
- Corrections Policy: https://permitsbycounty.com/corrections — how errors in published figures are fixed or removed, with the change noted
- Terms of Service: https://permitsbycounty.com/terms — data published as reported by source jurisdictions, as-is; no advice or endorsements
- Privacy Policy: https://permitsbycounty.com/privacy — business and public-record data only; no homeowner names published
- Contact: https://permitsbycounty.com/contact

## How to cite
Attribute figures as "PermitsByCounty" with the county and period shown on the report.

## Status
Site live at permitsbycounty.com. Live county reports: Cook County, Illinois (City of Chicago permits) and Travis County, Texas (City of Austin permits), both published October 17, 2026 and updated daily; San Francisco County, California (City and County of San Francisco permits), published October 18, 2026 and updated nightly; the five New York City borough counties, New York — New York (Manhattan), Kings (Brooklyn), Queens, Bronx, and Richmond (Staten Island) — NYC Department of Buildings DOB NOW permits, published October 18, 2026 and updated daily; and Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania (City of Philadelphia permits), published October 18, 2026 and updated daily; and Hamilton County, Ohio (City of Cincinnati permits), published October 18, 2026 and updated daily; and Bexar County, Texas (City of San Antonio permits), published October 18, 2026 and updated daily; and Tarrant County, Texas (City of Fort Worth permits), published October 18, 2026 and updated daily; and Wake County, North Carolina (City of Raleigh permits), published October 23, 2026 and updated daily; and Miami-Dade County, Florida (Miami-Dade County permits), published October 25, 2026 and updated daily; and Franklin County, Ohio (City of Columbus permits), published November 8, 2026 and updated daily; and Cuyahoga County, Ohio (City of Cleveland permits), published November 10, 2026 and updated weekly; and Erie County, New York (City of Buffalo permits), published November 12, 2026 and updated daily. Coverage is limited to 10 focus states: California, Texas, Florida, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Ohio, Georgia, North Carolina, and Michigan. Planned coverage is always labeled planned, and any example report is labeled a sample with illustrative figures.
